four experienced human judges, each with IMO-level mathematical expertise, were recruited to evaluate the responses
Evaluation began immediately after the 2025 IMO problems were released to prevent contamination.
each problem scored out of 7 points
each response was anonymized and graded independently by two judges
Each model was run with the recommended hyperparameters and a maximum token limit of 64,000.
For each problem, each model generated four distinct responses.
we applied a best-of-32 selection strategy using a method based on previous work
for each model solution, we first generated 32 responses
on average, each final model answer cost at least 3 dollars to generate, with Grok-4 costing over 20 dollars per answer
the performance reported here represents the models' best achievable output within a reasonable resource budget
In contrast, LLMs often received partial credit from our judges, especially on problem 4 and 5.
without the best-of-n filtering, model scores would likely have fallen below 10%

claiming that Gemini-2.5-Pro could achieve a gold medal with a specialized agentic framework. However, we have pointed out several issues with the paper methodology.
